claim: ACD-5 forms a homomeric acid-sensing ion channel.
source: ACD-5 can form a homomeric acid-sensing ion channel.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data from Xenopus oocytes showing pH-sensitive currents when ACD-5 is expressed alone (Figure 1C), and by the statement in the text.

claim: ACD-5 currents are inhibited by amiloride with an IC50 of 131μM.
source: Representative ACD-5 transients in Xenopus oocytes in the presence and absence of amiloride and (B) normalised amiloride-dose response curve (I/Imax as percentage) for ACD-5, showing a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 131μM (LogIC50=4.118) (N=8) indicated by the dashed line (curve fitted as described below).
evidence: The claim is directly supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 1B and described in the text.

claim: ACD-5 exhibits maximal current at around pH 6.
source: ACD-5 exhibited maximal current at around pH 6 and was inhibited by both higher and lower pH, with pH50s of 4.87 and 6.48 (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by pH-dose response curves shown in Figure 1C and stated in the text.

claim: ACD-5 is inhibited by pH 4.
source: ACD-5 exhibited maximal current at around pH 6 and was inhibited by both higher and lower pH, with pH50s of 4.87 and 6.48 (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by pH-dose response data in Figure 1C showing inhibition at pH 4.

claim: ACD-5 has an inhibitory pH50 of 4.87.
source: ACD-5 exhibited maximal current at around pH 6 and was inhibited by both higher and lower pH, with pH50s of 4.87 and 6.48 (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1C.

claim: ACD-5 has an excitatory pH50 of 6.48.
source: ACD-5 exhibited maximal current at around pH 6 and was inhibited by both higher and lower pH, with pH50s of 4.87 and 6.48 (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1C.

claim: ACD-5 shows a preference for Li+ over Na+.
source: ACD-5 shows a preference for Li+ over Na+ and a small preference of K+ over Na+ and is Ca2+ impermeable (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ion substitution experiments shown in Figure 1D and stated in the text.

claim: ACD-5 shows a small preference for K+ over Na+.
source: ACD-5 shows a preference for Li+ over Na+ and a small preference of K+ over Na+ and is Ca2+ impermeable (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ion substitution experiments shown in Figure 1D and stated in the text.

claim: ACD-5 is Ca2+ impermeable.
source: ACD-5 shows a preference for Li+ over Na+ and a small preference of K+ over Na+ and is Ca2+ impermeable (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ion substitution experiments shown in Figure 1D and stated in the text.

claim: ACD-5 is not permeable for protons.
source: ACD-5 was not permeable for protons, as the ΔErev did not show a positive shift when extracellular proton concentration was increased, and removal of Ca2+ from the solution also did not alter ΔErev.
evidence: The claim is supported by reversal potential measurements described in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Removal of Na+ from the solution induced a large negative ΔErev for ACD-5.
source: By contrast, removal of Na+ (by substituting with NMDG) induced a large negative ΔErev (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ion substitution data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: ACD-5 forms an amiloride-sensitive, pH-sensitive monovalent cation channel.
source: Thus, ACD-5 forms a homomeric amiloride-sensitive, pH-sensitive monovalent cation channel.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on multiple electrophysiological experiments described in the text and shown in Figure 1.

claim: acd-5(ok2657) is a truncation lacking TM2 and the C-terminus.
source: The only acd-5 mutation available was acd-5(ok2657), generated by the C. elegans Deletion Mutant Consortium (C. elegans Deletion Mutant Consortium, 2012), a truncation lacking TM2 and the C-terminus (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Oocytes expressing ACD-5(ok2657) alone did not display any currents.
source: Oocytes expressing ACD-5(ok2657) alone did not display any currents and were unaffected by amiloride (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Co-expressing ACD-5(ok2657) with wild-type ACD-5 significantly altered the expressed currents.
source: However, co-expressing ACD-5(ok2657) with wild-type ACD-5 significantly altered the expressed currents.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-expression experiments shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Increasing the ratio of injected acd-5(ok2657) cRNA to wild-type acd-5 cRNA resulted in a decrease in current.
source: Specifically, increasing the ratio of injected acd-5(ok2657) cRNA to wild-type acd-5 cRNA resulted in a decrease in current (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: ACD-5(ok2657) is a dominant mutation.
source: This suggests that the ACD-5(ok2657) subunit either forms a non-functional heteromer or sequesters factors required for wild-type ACD-5 function, and thus is a dominant mutation, hindering functional channel formation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the co-expression data in Figure 1E and further supported by behavioral data in Figure 3C.

claim: ACD-5 localises to the apical membrane of intestinal epithelial cells.
source: A translational acd-5::mKate2 C-terminal fusion showed expression in the intestinal epithelial cells, localising to the apical membrane, as confirmed by co-localisation with an apical membrane marker (OPT-2::GFP [Nehrke, 2003]) and by comparing the localisation with that of markers for the intestinal cytoplasm (Pdel-5::GFP) and lumen (ingested fluorescent dye, DiO) (Figure 1F and G and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1F, G and Figure 1—figure supplement 4, and by co-localization with known markers.

claim: The physiological pH environment of ACD-5 is likely in the range pH 4–6.
source: The observation that ACD-5 localises to the apical membrane indicated that its physiological environment is likely in the range pH 4–6, the pH range of the intestinal lumen (Pfeiffer et al., 2008; Chauhan et al., 2013), consistent with our electrophysiological findings that ACD-5 exhibits maximal current at pH 6 and is inhibited at pH 4.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the apical localization of ACD-5 and the known pH range of the intestinal lumen, supported by citations.

claim: acd-5 mutants show overall lower fluorescence intensities of Kansas Red, indicating a more neutral lumen pH compared to wild-type.
source: Mutants carrying either acd-5 allele showed overall lower fluorescence intensities, indicating a more neutral lumen pH compared to wild-type (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Kansas Red fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: In acd-5 mutants, the dye in the posterior part of the intestine was too faint to quantify.
source: In the acd-5 mutants, the dye in the posterior part of the intestine was too faint to quantify (in the non-fluorescent range of KR35 (pH 5.5–3.5)), this suggests that the increased luminal pH is a phenomenon that affects the whole intestinal lumen.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from Kansas Red imaging experiments described in the text and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The increased luminal pH in acd-5 mutants affects the whole intestinal lumen.
source: In the acd-5 mutants, the dye in the posterior part of the intestine was too faint to quantify (in the non-fluorescent range of KR35 (pH 5.5–3.5)), this suggests that the increased luminal pH is a phenomenon that affects the whole intestinal lumen.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the posterior intestine also shows reduced fluorescence, suggesting a global effect.

claim: ACD-5 localises to the luminal membrane throughout the intestine.
source: This is in line with the expression data that ACD-5 localises to the luminal membrane throughout the intestine.
evidence: The claim is consistent with the localization data shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: Only 61% of acd-5(lj122) mutants displayed at least one detectable MAT in a 2-min recording time.
source: As a result, both acd-5(lj122) and acd-5(ok2657) mutants exhibited a high incidence of missed (or undetectable) MATs, with only 61% and 56 %, respectively, displaying at least one detectable MAT in the 2-min recording time, compared with 82% of wild-type animals (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: Only 56% of acd-5(ok2657) mutants displayed at least one detectable MAT in a 2-min recording time.
source: As a result, both acd-5(lj122) and acd-5(ok2657) mutants exhibited a high incidence of missed (or undetectable) MATs, with only 61% and 56 %, respectively, displaying at least one detectable MAT in the 2-min recording time, compared with 82% of wild-type animals (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: 82% of wild-type animals displayed at least one detectable MAT in a 2-min recording time.
source: As a result, both acd-5(lj122) and acd-5(ok2657) mutants exhibited a high incidence of missed (or undetectable) MATs, with only 61% and 56 %, respectively, displaying at least one detectable MAT in the 2-min recording time, compared with 82% of wild-type animals (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: The defects in acd-5(lj122) null mutants were rescued by expression of the wild-type acd-5 gene.
source: These defects were rescued in the acd-5(lj122) null by expression of the wild-type acd-5 gene, but rescue was not observed for the truncated acd-5(ok2657) (Figure 2A, B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 2A, B, and C.

claim: Rescue was not observed for the truncated acd-5(ok2657) mutant.
source: These defects were rescued in the acd-5(lj122) null by expression of the wild-type acd-5 gene, but rescue was not observed for the truncated acd-5(ok2657) (Figure 2A, B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 2A, B, and C.

claim: MAT interval length was not grossly affected in acd-5 mutants where detectable.
source: Where detectable, MAT interval length was not grossly affected (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 2D showing no significant difference in MAT interval length.

claim: ACD-5 plays a pivotal role in the control of proton concentration.
source: Thus, although ACD-5 apparently plays a pivotal role in the control of proton concentration, it does not greatly influence the timing of the luminal proton wave.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that acd-5 mutants have altered luminal pH but normal MAT interval length.

claim: ACD-5 does not greatly influence the timing of the luminal proton wave.
source: Thus, although ACD-5 apparently plays a pivotal role in the control of proton concentration, it does not greatly influence the timing of the luminal proton wave.
evidence: The claim is supported by the observation that MAT interval length is not significantly affected in acd-5 mutants (Figure 2D).

claim: acd-5(ok2657) mutants displayed an increased amplitude of Ca2+ oscillations.
source: acd-5(ok2657) mutants showed an increased amplitude and significantly longer intervals between Ca2+ peaks, whereas acd-5(lj122) null animals displayed a reduced amplitude and a very small decrease in interval length (Figure 3A and B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1 for representative example traces).
evidence: The claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: acd-5(ok2657) mutants showed significantly longer intervals between Ca2+ peaks.
source: acd-5(ok2657) mutants showed an increased amplitude and significantly longer intervals between Ca2+ peaks, whereas acd-5(lj122) null animals displayed a reduced amplitude and a very small decrease in interval length (Figure 3A and B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1 for representative example traces).
evidence: The claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: acd-5(lj122) null animals displayed a reduced amplitude of Ca2+ oscillations.
source: acd-5(ok2657) mutants showed an increased amplitude and significantly longer intervals between Ca2+ peaks, whereas acd-5(lj122) null animals displayed a reduced amplitude and a very small decrease in interval length (Figure 3A and B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1 for representative example traces).
evidence: The claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: acd-5(lj122) null animals showed a very small decrease in Ca2+ interval length.
source: acd-5(ok2657) mutants showed an increased amplitude and significantly longer intervals between Ca2+ peaks, whereas acd-5(lj122) null animals displayed a reduced amplitude and a very small decrease in interval length (Figure 3A and B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1 for representative example traces).
evidence: The claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: acd-5 interacts with the Ca2+ oscillations.
source: This shows that acd-5 does interact with the Ca2+ oscillations, albeit in a relatively subtle manner.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed changes in Ca2+ oscillation amplitude and interval in acd-5 mutants.

claim: acd-5(ok2657) mutants exhibited significantly longer defecation cycle intervals.
source: The cycle intervals observed correspond well with the Ca2+ imaging observations; acd-5(ok2657) exhibited significantly longer intervals and acd-5(lj122) animals showed no difference from wild-type (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: acd-5(lj122) animals showed no difference from wild-type in defecation cycle intervals.
source: The cycle intervals observed correspond well with the Ca2+ imaging observations; acd-5(ok2657) exhibited significantly longer intervals and acd-5(lj122) animals showed no difference from wild-type (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Heterozygous acd-5(ok2657) animals retained the longer cycle phenotype.
source: Heterozygous animals and wild-type animals overexpressing the acd-5(ok2657) mutant gene, under the endogenous promoter or under another intestinal promoter (Pges-1) all retained the longer cycle phenotype, supporting this hypothesis (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Wild-type animals overexpressing the acd-5(ok2657) mutant gene retained the longer cycle phenotype.
source: Heterozygous animals and wild-type animals overexpressing the acd-5(ok2657) mutant gene, under the endogenous promoter or under another intestinal promoter (Pges-1) all retained the longer cycle phenotype, supporting this hypothesis (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Overexpression of the acd-5(ok2657) gene subtly increased variability.
source: We also found that overexpression of the acd-5(ok2657) gene subtly increased variability, although since this was also true of overexpression of the wild-type acd-5 gene (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B), it may have been a consequence of overexpression rather than the acd-5(ok2657) mutation itself.
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: Overexpression of the wild-type acd-5 gene also increased variability.
source: We also found that overexpression of the acd-5(ok2657) gene subtly increased variability, although since this was also true of overexpression of the wild-type acd-5 gene (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B), it may have been a consequence of overexpression rather than the acd-5(ok2657) mutation itself.
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: The IP3 receptor ITR-1 plays a critical role in the Ca2+ oscillations that drive the DMP.
source: The IP3 receptor, ITR-1, plays a critical role in the Ca2+ oscillations that drive the DMP and the loss-of-function allele itr-1(sa73) results in a dramatic increase in both cycle length and variability (Dal Santo et al., 1999; Walker et al., 2002; Espelt et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The loss-of-function allele itr-1(sa73) results in a dramatic increase in both cycle length and variability.
source: The IP3 receptor, ITR-1, plays a critical role in the Ca2+ oscillations that drive the DMP and the loss-of-function allele itr-1(sa73) results in a dramatic increase in both cycle length and variability (Dal Santo et al., 1999; Walker et al., 2002; Espelt et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and confirmed by data in Figure 3D and E.

claim: A compensatory effect is observed in itr-1(sa73) mutants where an aberrantly long cycle is followed by a short one, and vice versa.
source: We observed the previously described compensatory effect (Kwan et al., 2008) in itr-1(sa73), where an aberrantly long cycle is followed by a short one, and vice versa (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and a citation to a previous study.

claim: acd-5 alleles did not significantly reduce the cycle length or variability of itr-1(sa73).
source: Although the acd-5 alleles did not significantly reduce the cycle length or variability of itr-1(sa73), and the compensatory effect remained intact, we did nevertheless observe a striking suppression of excessively long cycles, with an almost complete loss of cycles over 200 s (Figure 3D and E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3A-C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 3D and E.

claim: acd-5 alleles suppressed excessively long cycles in itr-1(sa73) mutants, with an almost complete loss of cycles over 200 s.
source: Although the acd-5 alleles did not significantly reduce the cycle length or variability of itr-1(sa73), and the compensatory effect remained intact, we did nevertheless observe a striking suppression of excessively long cycles, with an almost complete loss of cycles over 200 s (Figure 3D and E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3A-C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 3D and E.

claim: The CV distribution was significantly different for both itr-1/acd-5 double mutants.
source: A Kolmogorov-Smirnov comparison of the cumulative distribution showed that cycle length distribution was not significantly different, but the CV distribution was significantly different for both itr-1/acd-5 double mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4B.

claim: acd-5 is responsible for the dysregulation that results in longer, more variable cycles in itr-1 mutants.
source: This suggests that acd-5 is responsible for the dysregulation that results in those longer, more variable cycles, perhaps suggesting a role for ACD-5 in regulating cycle length that is otherwise presumably masked or overridden by the dominant influence of the Ca2+ oscillator.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic interaction data between acd-5 and itr-1 mutants.

claim: The Na+/H+ exchanger PBO-4 localises to the basolateral membrane of the posterior intestinal cells.
source: The Na+/H+ exchanger PBO-4 localises to the basolateral membrane of the posterior intestinal cells, where it plays a central role in the release of protons into the pseudocoelom to trigger pBoc, and mutations result in missed or weak pBoc and frequently missed EMCs (Benomar et al., 2020; Beg et al., 2008; Pfeiffer et al., 2008), but the precise relationship between Ca2+ increase and PBO-4-mediated proton oscillations is unknown.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PBO-4 plays a central role in the release of protons into the pseudocoelom to trigger pBoc.
source: The Na+/H+ exchanger PBO-4 localises to the basolateral membrane of the posterior intestinal cells, where it plays a central role in the release of protons into the pseudocoelom to trigger pBoc, and mutations result in missed or weak pBoc and frequently missed EMCs (Benomar et al., 2020; Beg et al., 2008; Pfeiffer et al., 2008), but the precise relationship between Ca2+ increase and PBO-4-mediated proton oscillations is unknown.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: pbo-4 mutations result in missed or weak pBoc and frequently missed EMCs.
source: The Na+/H+ exchanger PBO-4 localises to the basolateral membrane of the posterior intestinal cells, where it plays a central role in the release of protons into the pseudocoelom to trigger pBoc, and mutations result in missed or weak pBoc and frequently missed EMCs (Benomar et al., 2020; Beg et al., 2008; Pfeiffer et al., 2008), but the precise relationship between Ca2+ increase and PBO-4-mediated proton oscillations is unknown.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and confirmed by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D-F.

claim: PBO-4 also localises to the apical membrane.
source: PBO-4 also localises to the apical membrane (Bender et al., 2013) but, as discussed earlier, its role there is controversial.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The pbo-4 mutation was dominant over the acd-5 mutations.
source: The pbo-4 mutation was dominant over the acd-5 mutations, with acd-5/pbo-4 double mutants both displaying wild-type cycle length and variability (like the pbo-4 single), and EMC and pBoc defects similar to the pbo-4 mutant (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3D-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic interaction data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 3D-F.

claim: acd-5/pbo-4 double mutants displayed wild-type cycle length and variability.
source: The pbo-4 mutation was dominant over the acd-5 mutations, with acd-5/pbo-4 double mutants both displaying wild-type cycle length and variability (like the pbo-4 single), and EMC and pBoc defects similar to the pbo-4 mutant (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3D-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 3F.

claim: acd-5/pbo-4 double mutants showed EMC and pBoc defects similar to the pbo-4 mutant.
source: The pbo-4 mutation was dominant over the acd-5 mutations, with acd-5/pbo-4 double mutants both displaying wild-type cycle length and variability (like the pbo-4 single), and EMC and pBoc defects similar to the pbo-4 mutant (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3D-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D-F.

claim: pbo-4 acts genetically upstream of acd-5.
source: This is consistent with pbo-4 acting genetically upstream of acd-5; however, this could reflect an apical role for PBO-4 (Figure 3G) or simply the dominance of basolateral proton release in driving downstream events.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic interaction data, though alternative explanations are acknowledged.

claim: FLR-1 was shown to localise to both apical and basolateral membranes.
source: Previous research identified the expression of another DEG/ENaC channel gene, flr-1, in the intestine (Take-uchi et al., 1998), and it was shown to localise to both apical and basolateral membranes (Take-uchi et al., 1998; Kobayashi et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: flr-1 mutants show more severe disruption of the DMP than acd-5 mutants.
source: flr-1 mutants show more severe disruption of the DMP than acd-5 mutants, leading us to hypothesise that there might be two distinct channels in the intestinal cell: A heteromeric or homomeric ACD-5-containing channel on the apical membrane and an FLR-1-containing channel on both membranes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing the phenotypes of flr-1 and acd-5 mutants.

claim: FLR-1 expressed alone in oocytes did not produce pH-sensitive currents.
source: Since FLR-1 expressed alone in oocytes did not produce pH-sensitive currents in our experiments, we hypothesised that FLR-1 could contribute to a heteromeric channel.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: acd-3 and del-5 are expressed in the intestine.
source: Therefore, we used transcriptional fusions to search for additional intestinally expressed DEG/ENaCs. We found two such intestine-expressed genes, acd-3 and del-5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptional reporter data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: ACD-5 and FLR-1 share the highest homology with mammalian ASIC2.
source: Whereas ACD-5 and FLR-1 share the highest homology with mammalian ASIC2, ACD-3 shares the highest homology with mammalian ASIC5 and DEL-5 is more distantly related.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence homology analysis, which is a standard bioinformatics approach.

claim: ACD-3 shares the highest homology with mammalian ASIC5.
source: Whereas ACD-5 and FLR-1 share the highest homology with mammalian ASIC2, ACD-3 shares the highest homology with mammalian ASIC5 and DEL-5 is more distantly related.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence homology analysis.

claim: DEL-5 is more distantly related to mammalian ASICs.
source: Whereas ACD-5 and FLR-1 share the highest homology with mammalian ASIC2, ACD-3 shares the highest homology with mammalian ASIC5 and DEL-5 is more distantly related.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence homology analysis.

claim: mKate::DEL-5 and ACD-3::mKate2 showed evidence of basolateral localisation.
source: We investigated the subcellular localisation of ACD-3 and DEL-5 using translational fusions. In common with FLR-1::GFP (Take-uchi et al., 1998), mKate::DEL-5 and ACD-3::mKate2, where detectable, showed a diffuse distribution. Where expression levels were more variable, we were able to observe evidence of basolateral localisation, but we cannot exclude that DEL-5 and ACD-3 are also apically localised, since this could potentially be masked (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Co-expression of FLR-1 with either DEL-5, ACD-3, or both resulted in a response to changes in pH from a holding pH 5.
source: However, when we co-expressed FLR-1 with either DEL-5, ACD-3, or both, we observed a response to changes in pH from a holding pH 5 (pH50 of 6.42), a profile resembling that previously reported for the TadNaCs, DEG/ENaC channels of the marine placozoa Trichoplax adhaerens (Elkhatib et al., 2019; Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 4A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 heteromeric channel has a pH50 of 6.42.
source: However, when we co-expressed FLR-1 with either DEL-5, ACD-3, or both, we observed a response to changes in pH from a holding pH 5 (pH50 of 6.42), a profile resembling that previously reported for the TadNaCs, DEG/ENaC channels of the marine placozoa Trichoplax adhaerens (Elkhatib et al., 2019; Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 4A,B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4D.

claim: No currents were detected in response to pH when expressing DEL-5 together with ACD-3.
source: We could not detect any currents in response to pH when expressing DEL-5 together with ACD-3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4C.

claim: The pH50s did not change when FLR-1 (ACD-3 or DEL-5) was co-expressed with ACD-5 compared to the expression of ACD-5 alone.
source: As FLR-1 has previously been proposed to localise at both the basolateral and luminal intestinal membrane (Take-uchi et al., 1998; Kobayashi et al., 2011), where it might form heteromers with ACD-5, we also co-expressed FLR-1 (ACD-3 or DEL-5) with ACD-5 in oocytes. The pH50s did not change compared to the expression of ACD-5 alone (Figure 4—figure supplement 5A,B,).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: The other subunits do not influence ACD-5 channel function.
source: Co-expression can be difficult to interpret, due to the potential presence of a mix of homo-and heteromeric channels, which can confound whole-cell recordings (Hesselager et al., 2004). However, our results suggest that the other subunits do not influence ACD-5 channel function.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the co-expression data, though the authors acknowledge the limitations of this approach.

claim: The heteromeric FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel is insensitive to amiloride.
source: We also tested amiloride sensitivity of this heteromeric channel and found that it is insensitive to the blocker (Figure 4E), a phenomenon previously reported for a mutant DEGT-1 channel (Fechner et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4E and a citation to a previous study.

claim: The heteromeric FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel did not show a significant shift in ΔErev between the monovalent cations.
source: We next investigated ion selectivity, the heteromeric FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel did not show a significant shift in ΔErev between the monovalent cations, however, it showed a negative shift in ΔErev when switching to a CaCl2 solution with some current remaining (Figure 4F–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by ion substitution data shown in Figure 4F and G.

claim: The heteromeric FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel showed a negative shift in ΔErev when switching to a CaCl2 solution with some current remaining.
source: We next investigated ion selectivity, the heteromeric FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel did not show a significant shift in ΔErev between the monovalent cations, however, it showed a negative shift in ΔErev when switching to a CaCl2 solution with some current remaining (Figure 4F–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by ion substitution data shown in Figure 4F and G.

claim: The heteromeric FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel is marginally permeable for Ca2+.
source: This suggests that the channel is also marginally permeable for Ca2+.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of a negative shift in ΔErev with CaCl2 and some remaining current.

claim: Removal of Na+ (by substituting with NMDG) induced a negative shift in ΔErev for the FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel.
source: Removal of Na+ (by substituting with NMDG) also induced a negative shift in ΔErev (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by ion substitution data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: FLR-1, together with ACD-3 and/or DEL-5, forms a functional amiloride-insensitive acid-inhibited channel with different properties to ACD-5.
source: Thus, FLR-1, together with ACD-3 and/or DEL-5, appears to form a functional amiloride-insensitive acid-inhibited channel with different properties to ACD-5.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the electrophysiological characterization of the FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel.

claim: There is a second intestinal DEG/ENaC, an FLR-1, ACD-3, and DEL-5-containing heteromeric channel localised to the basolateral membrane.
source: These findings support the hypothesis that there is a second intestinal DEG/ENaC, an FLR-1, ACD-3, and DEL-5-containing heteromeric channel localised to the basolateral membrane.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on localization and electrophysiological data.

claim: flr-1(ut11) mutants show high variability of DMP cycle length, with many extremely short cycles (less than 30 s).
source: flr-1(ut11) mutants show high variability of DMP cycle length, with many extremely short cycles (less than 30 s) (Katsura et al., 1994; Take-uchi et al., 1998; Kwan et al., 2008; Take-uchi et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and confirmed by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: flr-1(syb3521) is a truncation of the N-terminus and predicted TM1 with the remaining gene being out of frame so no protein is generated.
source: We created flr-1(syb3521), using CRISPR/Cas9 (Dokshin et al., 2018), truncating the N-terminus and predicted TM1 with the remaining gene being out of frame so no protein is generated (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, D.

claim: flr-1(syb3521) presented with a slow-growing, caloric restriction-like phenotype.
source: As previously described for flr-1(ut11) and other alleles (Katsura et al., 1994; Take-uchi et al., 1998; Kobayashi et al., 2011), syb3521 presented with a slow-growing, caloric restriction-like phenotype and were thus difficult to cross.
evidence: The claim is supported by observations and citations to previous studies.

claim: flr-1(RNAi) animals exhibited the caloric restriction phenotype.
source: As expected, flr-1(RNAi) animals also exhibited the caloric restriction phenotype.
evidence: The claim is based on observations of RNAi-treated animals.

claim: flr-1(RNAi) and flr-1(syb3521) animals showed disruption of DMP, with a dramatic increase in variability, a mix of extremely short and long cycles, missed EMCs and missed or weak pBoc contractions.
source: Like flr-1(ut11), both flr-1(RNAi) and flr-1(syb3521) animals showed disruption of DMP, with a dramatic increase in variability, a mix of extremely short and long cycles, missed EMCs and missed or weak pBoc contractions (Figure 5A–D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5A-D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: acd-3/del-5 double mutants phenocopied the flr-1 deficient animals.
source: Interestingly, acd-3/del-5 double mutants phenocopied the flr-1 deficient animals, showing similar defects in cycle length, EMC and pBoc defects (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5A-D.

claim: flr-1(RNAi) did not significantly alter the phenotypes of acd-3/del-5 double mutants.
source: flr-1(RNAi) did not significantly alter these phenotypes, suggesting that the three genes function together and further supporting the hypothesis that these three subunits form a heteromer.
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic interaction data shown in Figure 5A-E.

claim: The three genes flr-1, acd-3, and del-5 function together.
source: flr-1(RNAi) did not significantly alter these phenotypes, suggesting that the three genes function together and further supporting the hypothesis that these three subunits form a heteromer.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic interaction data.

claim: Neither of the acd-3 or del-5 single mutants exhibited phenotypes similar to acd-3/del-5 double mutants.
source: Neither of the acd-3 or del-5 single mutants exhibited such phenotypes, suggesting that they act redundantly.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that single mutants have no phenotype while double mutants do.

claim: acd-3 and del-5 act redundantly.
source: Neither of the acd-3 or del-5 single mutants exhibited such phenotypes, suggesting that they act redundantly.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic data.

claim: The defects observed for acd-3/del-5 double mutants were rescued by expression of the acd-3::mKate2 or mKate2::del-5 fusions.
source: The defects observed for acd-3/del-5 double mutants were rescued by expression of the acd-3::mKate2 or mKate2::del-5 fusions (Figure 5—figure supplement 3, Table 1), confirming that their functionality is retained and thus that the localisation observed in Figure 4A is functionally relevant.
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3 and Table 1.

claim: Both the flr-1 deficient animals and the acd-3/del-5 double mutants frequently exhibited short <17 s cycles, described as 'echos'.
source: Both the flr-1 deficient animals and the acd-3/del-5 double mutants frequently exhibited short <17 s cycles, seen for unc-43(sa200) CaMK II mutants and described as 'echos', since they are often incomplete (missing EMC) (Teramoto and Iwasaki, 2006; Liu and Thomas, 1994; Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5E and citations to previous studies.

claim: Expression of either acd-3 or del-5 under an intestine-specific promoter significantly rescues all of the defects exhibited by acd-3/del-5 double mutants.
source: As Figure 5—figure supplement 3 shows, expression of either acd-3 or del-5 under an intestine-specific promoter significantly rescues all of the defects exhibited by acd-3/del-5 double mutants, supporting the idea that the intestine is the site of function.
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: The intestine is the site of function for acd-3 and del-5.
source: As Figure 5—figure supplement 3 shows, expression of either acd-3 or del-5 under an intestine-specific promoter significantly rescues all of the defects exhibited by acd-3/del-5 double mutants, supporting the idea that the intestine is the site of function.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the rescue experiments.

claim: flr-1 is expressed only in the intestine.
source: This coincides with previous observations that flr-1 is expressed only in the intestine, and that an intestinally expressed fusion rescues the flr-1 mutant phenotype (Take-uchi et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: An intestinally expressed fusion rescues the flr-1 mutant phenotype.
source: This coincides with previous observations that flr-1 is expressed only in the intestine, and that an intestinally expressed fusion rescues the flr-1 mutant phenotype (Take-uchi et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Interrupting the Ca2+ wave with heparin in parts of the intestine eliminates the aBoc and EMC following the pBoc.
source: Previous research has shown that interrupting the Ca2+ wave with heparin, an IP3 receptor inhibitor, in parts of the intestine eliminates the aBoc and EMC following the pBoc, suggesting that the Ca2+ wave is upstream of these steps (Teramoto and Iwasaki, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The Ca2+ wave is upstream of aBoc and EMC.
source: Previous research has shown that interrupting the Ca2+ wave with heparin, an IP3 receptor inhibitor, in parts of the intestine eliminates the aBoc and EMC following the pBoc, suggesting that the Ca2+ wave is upstream of these steps (Teramoto and Iwasaki, 2006).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the heparin experiment cited.

claim: The acd-3/del-5 and flr-1 mutations are likely to interfere with the intestinal Ca2+ wave.
source: The similarities with both the itr-1 (highly variable, long cycles), and unc-43 (echos) phenotypes suggests that the acd-3/del-5 and flr-1 mutations are likely to interfere with the intestinal Ca2+ wave.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the phenotypic similarities to itr-1 and unc-43 mutants.

claim: flr-1(syb3521) completely disrupted the rhythmicity of Ca2+ oscillations.
source: As Figure 6 shows, flr-1(syb3521) completely disrupted the rhythmicity of Ca2+ oscillations that we normally observe in wild-type animals (see Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2 for additional traces).
evidence: The claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging data shown in Figure 6 and supplementary figures.

claim: Both the basal and maximal Ca2+ concentrations were significantly decreased in flr-1(syb3521) mutants.
source: Overall, both the basal and maximal Ca2+ concentrations were significantly decreased (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: FLR-1 functions in a heteromer along with ACD-3 and/or DEL-5.
source: Taken together, our data indicate that FLR-1 functions in a heteromer along with ACD-3 and/or DEL-5 and that this/these proton-gated channels, exposed to the pseudocoelom, play a major role in controlling the intestinal Ca2+ transients that are so central to the DMP.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on genetic and electrophysiological data.

claim: The FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 proton-gated channels play a major role in controlling the intestinal Ca2+ transients that are central to the DMP.
source: Taken together, our data indicate that FLR-1 functions in a heteromer along with ACD-3 and/or DEL-5 and that this/these proton-gated channels, exposed to the pseudocoelom, play a major role in controlling the intestinal Ca2+ transients that are so central to the DMP.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on genetic and Ca2+ imaging data.

claim: flr-1(RNAi) impacted both intracellular and pseudocoelomic pH.
source: As Figure 7 shows, flr-1(RNAi) impacted both intracellular and pseudocoelomic pH.
evidence: The claim is supported by pH imaging data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Basal intracellular pH was unaffected in flr-1(RNAi) animals.
source: Whereas basal intracellular pH was unaffected, the acidification that accompanies pBoc was not as extensive (Figure 7A–C, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by pH imaging data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The acidification that accompanies pBoc was not as extensive in flr-1(RNAi) animals.
source: Whereas basal intracellular pH was unaffected, the acidification that accompanies pBoc was not as extensive (Figure 7A–C, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by pH imaging data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Basal pseudocoelomic pH was unaffected in flr-1(RNAi) animals.
source: Likewise, consistent with the role of intracellular acidification in triggering proton release into the pseudocoelom (Beg et al., 2008; Pfeiffer et al., 2008), basal pseudocoelomic pH was unaffected, but the acidification (which triggers pBoc) was severely attenuated (Figure 7D–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by pH imaging data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The acidification of the pseudocoelom (which triggers pBoc) was severely attenuated in flr-1(RNAi) animals.
source: Likewise, consistent with the role of intracellular acidification in triggering proton release into the pseudocoelom (Beg et al., 2008; Pfeiffer et al., 2008), basal pseudocoelomic pH was unaffected, but the acidification (which triggers pBoc) was severely attenuated (Figure 7D–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by pH imaging data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Evidence of oscillations with a shorter periodicity was observed in flr-1(RNAi) animals, corresponding with the <17 s cycles and shorter interval Ca2+ fluctuations.
source: Interestingly, we also observed evidence of oscillations with a shorter periodicity, corresponding with the <17 s cycles and sorter interval Ca2+ fluctuations.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from pH imaging data shown in Figure 7.

claim: In controlling intracellular Ca2+, the FLR-1-containing channel also controls proton release and thus pseudocoelomic pH.
source: Our findings demonstrate that, in controlling intracellular Ca2+, the FLR-1-containing channel also controls proton release and thus pseudocoelomic pH, explaining the defects in pBoc.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on Ca2+ and pH imaging data.

claim: Many of the physiological changes associated with dysregulation of intestinal lumen pH reflect starvation, including developmental delay or arrest and reduced growth rate.
source: Many of the physiological changes associated with dysregulation of intestinal lumen pH reflect starvation, including developmental delay or arrest and reduced growth rate (Benomar et al., 2020; Allman et al., 2009; Pfeiffer et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: These characteristics resemble the phenotypes that have previously been described for flr-1 mutants.
source: These characteristics resemble the phenotypes that have previously been described for flr-1 mutants (Take-uchi et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: acd-3/del-5 mutants had an appearance suggesting caloric restriction.
source: We noticed that the acd-3/del-5 mutants also had an appearance suggesting caloric restriction, whereas the single acd-3 and del-5 mutants had a superficially normal appearance (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on visual observations shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Single acd-3 and del-5 mutants had a superficially normal appearance.
source: We noticed that the acd-3/del-5 mutants also had an appearance suggesting caloric restriction, whereas the single acd-3 and del-5 mutants had a superficially normal appearance (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on visual observations shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Wild-type and acd-5(lj122) mutants showed similar developmental timescales (median 74 and 74 hr).
source: Wild-type and the acd-5(lj122) mutants showed similar developmental timescales (median 74 and 74 hr), while there was a small but statistically significant delay in developmental timing for the acd-5(ok2657), acd-3(ok1335), and del-5(lj138) (median 75, 79, and 78 hr, respectively) (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by developmental timing data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: There was a small but statistically significant delay in developmental timing for acd-5(ok2657), acd-3(ok1335), and del-5(lj138) (median 75, 79, and 78 hr, respectively).
source: Wild-type and the acd-5(lj122) mutants showed similar developmental timescales (median 74 and 74 hr), while there was a small but statistically significant delay in developmental timing for the acd-5(ok2657), acd-3(ok1335), and del-5(lj138) (median 75, 79, and 78 hr, respectively) (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by developmental timing data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: flr-1(syb3521) single mutants and acd-3/del-5 double mutants showed a severe developmental delay, taking three times as long to reach adulthood.
source: By contrast, the flr-1(syb3521) single mutants and the acd-3/del-5 double mutants showed a severe developmental delay, taking three times as long to reach adulthood (Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is supported by developmental timing data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: A small fraction of flr-1(syb3521) and acd-3/del-5 mutants arrested and died as larvae or before egg-laying.
source: A small fraction of these animals arrested and died as larvae or before egg-laying.
evidence: The claim is based on observations during developmental timing experiments.

claim: acd-3, acd-5, and del-5 single mutants show a wild-type length.
source: When we quantified the size of day-1 adults, we found that the acd-3, acd-5, and del-5 single mutants show a wild-type length; by contrast, flr-1(syb3521) single mutants and the acd-3/del-5 double mutants are significantly shorter (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is supported by body size measurements shown in Figure 8C.

claim: flr-1(syb3521) single mutants and acd-3/del-5 double mutants are significantly shorter.
source: When we quantified the size of day-1 adults, we found that the acd-3, acd-5, and del-5 single mutants show a wild-type length; by contrast, flr-1(syb3521) single mutants and the acd-3/del-5 double mutants are significantly shorter (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is supported by body size measurements shown in Figure 8C.

claim: These phenotypes are consistent with a role for FLR-1, ACD-3, and DEL-5 in development and growth.
source: These phenotypes are consistent with a role for FLR-1, ACD-3, and DEL-5 in development and growth.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the developmental and growth defects observed in the mutants.

claim: Peptide absorption is dependent on proton gradients where nutrients are taken up against the gradient and greatly enhanced at a low extracellular pH.
source: Peptide absorption is dependent on proton gradients where nutrients are taken up against the gradient and greatly enhanced at a low extracellular pH (Mackenzie et al., 1996; Fei et al., 1994; Liang et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In C. elegans, the proton gradient is known to drive nutrient uptake via the OPT-2/PEP-2, a proton-coupled oligopeptide transporter.
source: In C. elegans, the proton gradient is known to drive nutrient uptake via the OPT-2/PEP-2, a proton-coupled oligopeptide transporter, which is also involved in fat accumulation and opt-2 mutants show a decrease in intestinal fat deposits (Nehrke, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: opt-2 mutants show a decrease in intestinal fat deposits.
source: In C. elegans, the proton gradient is known to drive nutrient uptake via the OPT-2/PEP-2, a proton-coupled oligopeptide transporter, which is also involved in fat accumulation and opt-2 mutants show a decrease in intestinal fat deposits (Nehrke, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Previous research revealed a link between DMP defects and aberrant fat metabolism.
source: Previous research revealed a link between DMP defects and aberrant fat metabolism, as well as between dysregulation of intestinal pH and reduced fat storage resulting in nutrient uptake deficiency (Sheng et al., 2015; Allman et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Dysregulation of intestinal pH is linked to reduced fat storage resulting in nutrient uptake deficiency.
source: Previous research revealed a link between DMP defects and aberrant fat metabolism, as well as between dysregulation of intestinal pH and reduced fat storage resulting in nutrient uptake deficiency (Sheng et al., 2015; Allman et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: flr-1 single and acd-3/del-5 double mutants showed a clear reduction in intestinal fat accumulation, indicated by reduced Oil-Red O staining.
source: We found a clear reduction in intestinal fat accumulation, indicated by reduced Oil-Red O staining in flr-1 single and acd-3/del-5 double mutants, demonstrating aberrant fat metabolism (Figure 8D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Oil-Red O staining data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: flr-1 single and acd-3/del-5 double mutants demonstrate aberrant fat metabolism.
source: We found a clear reduction in intestinal fat accumulation, indicated by reduced Oil-Red O staining in flr-1 single and acd-3/del-5 double mutants, demonstrating aberrant fat metabolism (Figure 8D).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the reduced fat staining observed.

claim: The reduced fat accumulation is consistent with the reduced growth rate and decreased body size.
source: This is consistent with the reduced growth rate and decreased body size and underlines the importance of proper regulation of the DMP, by the FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation between fat metabolism, growth, and body size.

claim: Proper regulation of the DMP by the FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel is important.
source: This is consistent with the reduced growth rate and decreased body size and underlines the importance of proper regulation of the DMP, by the FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the observed phenotypes.

claim: There are two acid-sensitive DEG/ENaC channels with distinct functions.
source: Using a combination of electrophysiology, behavioural analysis, genetic manipulations, and pH and Ca2+ indicator imaging, we have obtained evidence for two acid-sensitive DEG/ENaC channels with distinct functions (Figure 9).
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on all the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: One channel includes ACD-5, which localises to the luminal membrane and is the main proton sensing subunit of the channel.
source: One includes ACD-5, which localises to the luminal membrane and is the main proton sensing subunit of the channel.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the ACD-5 characterization.

claim: The ACD-5 proton sensor is required for maintenance and/or establishment of acidic luminal pH.
source: This proton sensor is required for maintenance and/or establishment of acidic luminal pH and yet only subtly influences the DMP, and the Ca2+ oscillator.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the ACD-5 functional analysis.

claim: The ACD-5 proton sensor only subtly influences the DMP and the Ca2+ oscillator.
source: This proton sensor is required for maintenance and/or establishment of acidic luminal pH and yet only subtly influences the DMP, and the Ca2+ oscillator.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the ACD-5 functional analysis.

claim: The second channel is composed of FLR-1, ACD-3, and/or DEL-5, localises to the basolateral membrane and is essential for timing and execution of DMP muscle contractions.
source: The second, composed of FLR-1, ACD-3, and/or DEL-5, localises to the basolateral membrane and is essential for timing and execution of DMP muscle contractions, with consequences for fat metabolism and growth.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 characterization.

claim: The FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 channel has consequences for fat metabolism and growth.
source: The second, composed of FLR-1, ACD-3, and/or DEL-5, localises to the basolateral membrane and is essential for timing and execution of DMP muscle contractions, with consequences for fat metabolism and growth.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 functional analysis.

claim: ACD-5 and FLR-1-containing channels exhibit very different pH dependence and kinetics.
source: ACD-5 and FLR-1-containing channels exhibit very different pH dependence and kinetics; ACD-5 is fully open at pH 6 and closed at pH 4, reflecting the range of pH oscillations in the lumen (Allman et al., 2009), whereas FLR-1-containing heteromers form a proton-inhibited cation leak channel, similar to ACD-1, TadNaC6 and vertebrate ASIC5 (Wang et al., 2008; Elkhatib et al., 2019; Wiemuth and Gründer, 2010).
evidence: The claim is a summary comparison of the two channels, supported by data and citations.

claim: FLR-1-containing heteromers form a proton-inhibited cation leak channel, similar to ACD-1, TadNaC6 and vertebrate ASIC5.
source: ACD-5 and FLR-1-containing channels exhibit very different pH dependence and kinetics; ACD-5 is fully open at pH 6 and closed at pH 4, reflecting the range of pH oscillations in the lumen (Allman et al., 2009), whereas FLR-1-containing heteromers form a proton-inhibited cation leak channel, similar to ACD-1, TadNaC6 and vertebrate ASIC5 (Wang et al., 2008; Elkhatib et al., 2019; Wiemuth and Gründer, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data and citations to previous studies.

claim: The pH dependence of human ENaCs reflects the pH range in epithelia where they are expressed.
source: This presumably reflects their different physiological contexts, just as the pH dependence of human ENaCs reflects the pH range in epithelia where they are expressed (Collier and Snyder, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Neither ACD-5 nor FLR-1 currents desensitise; the channel remains open for the duration of the pH stimulus.
source: Neither ACD-5 nor FLR-1 currents desensitise; the channel remains open for the duration of the pH stimulus (although we see some evidence of partial desensitisation of FLR-1 at certain pHs).
evidence: The claim is based on observations from electrophysiological recordings.

claim: The lack of desensitization contrasts with the fast desensitisation of mammalian ASICs and is more analogous to the slower kinetics of ENaCs.
source: This contrasts with the fast desensitisation of mammalian ASICs and is more analogous to the slower kinetics of ENaCs.
evidence: The claim is a comparison based on knowledge of mammalian ASICs and ENaCs.

claim: ACD-5 activation ensures a return to the condition (pH~4) at which it is closed.
source: It coincides well with our evidence that ACD-5 is actually required for establishment or maintenance of acidic luminal pH; that is, its activation ensures a return to the condition (pH~4) at which it is closed.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the functional role of ACD-5 in maintaining luminal pH.

claim: The FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 heteromeric channel on the basolateral membrane is predicted to be constitutively open as the extracellular resting pH is around 7.35.
source: By contrast, the FLR-1/ACD-3/DEL-5 heteromeric channel on the basolateral membrane is predicted to be constitutively open as the extracellular resting pH is around 7.35 (Allman et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the pH dependence of the channel and the known pH of the pseudocoelom.

claim: All four intestinal DEG/ENaC subunits influence the DMP, but the degree of influence differs dramatically.
source: All four intestinal DEG/ENaC subunits influence the DMP, but the degree of influence differs dramatically, providing us with mechanistic information about the relationships between extracellular and intracellular events.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the genetic analysis of the four subunits.

claim: Intestinal IP3-dependent Ca2+ signalling acts as the master oscillator and is responsible for cycle length and timing.
source: Research to date indicates that intestinal IP3-dependent Ca2+ signalling act as the master oscillator and is responsible for cycle length and timing.
evidence: The claim is a summary of previous research, supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Disrupting IP3 signalling results in a dramatic lengthening and disruption of rhythmicity of the DMP.
source: Disrupting IP3 signalling results in a dramatic lengthening and disruption of rhythmicity of the DMP, and a direct relationship is seen between the timing of Ca2+ fluctuations and the DMP (Kwan et al., 2008; Walker et al., 2002; Espelt et al., 2005; Teramoto and Iwasaki, 2006; Dal Santo et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A direct relationship is seen between the timing of Ca2+ fluctuations and the DMP.
source: Disrupting IP3 signalling results in a dramatic lengthening and disruption of rhythmicity of the DMP, and a direct relationship is seen between the timing of Ca2+ fluctuations and the DMP (Kwan et al., 2008; Walker et al., 2002; Espelt et al., 2005; Teramoto and Iwasaki, 2006; Dal Santo et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The acd-5 mutant data supports the hypothesis that the Ca2+ oscillator is dominant.
source: Our acd-5 mutant data supports this hypothesis; the underlying Ca2+ fluctuations, and DMP rhythmicity, were only subtly affected, despite dramatic disruption of luminal pH, underlining the dominance of the Ca2+ oscillator.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the acd-5 mutant phenotypes.

claim: ACD-5 is not responsible for the timing of the proton wave, but acts downstream.
source: Where detectable, the MAT interval length was also not affected, suggesting that ACD-5 is not responsible for the timing of the proton wave, but acts downstream.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that MAT interval is not affected in acd-5 mutants.

claim: There is a functional link between ACD-5 and VHA-6.
source: This is supported by the phenotype of animals deficient in the V-ATPase, VHA-6; lumen pH remained more neutral, but robust Ca2+ oscillations were maintained, with only a small increase in cycle length (similar to acd-5(ok2657)) (Allman et al., 2009). This suggests a functional link between the two; a pH~6-activated cation channel and a presumed H+ pump whose effect would be to acidify the lumen, although the vha-6 phenotype is more severe than acd-5, interfering with nutrient uptake and growth rate, indicating that there is not a complete overlap in their roles.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the phenotypic similarities between acd-5 and vha-6 mutants, supported by a citation.

claim: The vha-6 phenotype is more severe than acd-5, interfering with nutrient uptake and growth rate.
source: This is supported by the phenotype of animals deficient in the V-ATPase, VHA-6; lumen pH remained more neutral, but robust Ca2+ oscillations were maintained, with only a small increase in cycle length (similar to acd-5(ok2657)) (Allman et al., 2009). This suggests a functional link between the two; a pH~6-activated cation channel and a presumed H+ pump whose effect would be to acidify the lumen, although the vha-6 phenotype is more severe than acd-5, interfering with nutrient uptake and growth rate, indicating that there is not a complete overlap in their roles.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: There is not a complete overlap in the roles of ACD-5 and VHA-6.
source: This is supported by the phenotype of animals deficient in the V-ATPase, VHA-6; lumen pH remained more neutral, but robust Ca2+ oscillations were maintained, with only a small increase in cycle length (similar to acd-5(ok2657)) (Allman et al., 2009). This suggests a functional link between the two; a pH~6-activated cation channel and a presumed H+ pump whose effect would be to acidify the lumen, although the vha-6 phenotype is more severe than acd-5, interfering with nutrient uptake and growth rate, indicating that there is not a complete overlap in their roles.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differences in phenotypic severity.

claim: The Ca2+ oscillator is largely unperturbed in acd-5 mutants.
source: Whatever the mechanism, it is clear that the Ca2+ oscillator is largely unperturbed.
evidence: The claim is a summary of the acd-5 mutant Ca2+ imaging data.

claim: When the Ca2+ oscillator is disrupted, in itr-1 deficient animals, the very long cycles observed are dependent on acd-5.
source: We do nevertheless see some influence; in particular, when the Ca2+ oscillator is disrupted, in itr-1 deficient animals, the very long cycles observed are dependent on acd-5, revealing an otherwise constraining role.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic interaction between acd-5 and itr-1.

claim: ACD-5 has an otherwise constraining role on cycle length.
source: We do nevertheless see some influence; in particular, when the Ca2+ oscillator is disrupted, in itr-1 deficient animals, the very long cycles observed are dependent on acd-5, revealing an otherwise constraining role.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic interaction data.

claim: The Ca2+ oscillator is upstream, and/or largely independent, of lumen pH.
source: The Ca2+ oscillator is thus upstream, and/or largely independent, of lumen pH, and is the dominant force driving DMP rhythmicity.

claim: The Ca2+ oscillator is the dominant force driving DMP rhythmicity.
